harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent internal DNS on node1 and node2. After sequentially rebooting both nodes, `inventory-api.internal` still resolves through node1 to node2 at 10.100.166.11. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Configured preinstalled dnsmasq 2.45 on node1 to listen at 10.100.166.10:53, serve the internal record, and forward other queries upstream.
Enabled dnsmasq at boot and persisted subnet-scoped TCP/UDP DNS firewall rules.
Configured node2's active and persistent resolver settings to use 10.100.166.10.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, verifying changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 runs an internal resolver mapping inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq is enabled and running, listens on TCP/UDP 10.100.166.10:53, and answers 10.100.166.11. Firewall rules are persisted.

evidence.requirement: node2 uses node1 for internal lookups
evidence.summary: Active and persistent resolver settings point to 10.100.166.10; system and direct DNS queries return 10.100.166.11 from that server.

evidence.requirement: Legacy OS release and kernel retained
